enonce.texte:
Identify the correct relative pronoun to complete each sentence: who, which, that, whose.

1. The man _______ is standing there is my uncle.

2. The book _______ I read was very interesting.

3. The woman _______ car was stolen called the police.

4. This is the house _______ I grew up.

5. The movie _______ we watched last night was amazing.

questions.texte: Choose the correct relative pronoun for each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. who, 2. which/that, 3. whose, 4. where (or which/that), 5. which/that

enonce.texte:
Read the sentences and identify if the relative clause is defining or non-defining. Add commas where necessary.

1. "My sister who lives in London is a doctor." → _______

2. "The book which I bought yesterday is on the table." → _______

3. "Mr. Smith who is our manager will attend the meeting." → _______

4. "The students who passed the exam will receive a certificate." → _______

5. "Paris which is the capital of France is a beautiful city." → _______

questions.texte: Identify each clause as defining or non-defining.
questions.reponse: 1. Defining (no commas), 2. Defining (no commas), 3. Non-defining (add commas around the clause), 4. Defining (no commas), 5. Non-defining (add commas around the clause)

enonce.texte:
Combine each pair of sentences into one sentence using a relative clause.

1. The woman is a doctor. She lives next door.

2. The book is very interesting. I bought it yesterday.

3. The man called the police. His car was stolen.

4. The hotel was very comfortable. We stayed there last summer.

5. The teacher is very kind. She teaches English.

questions.texte: Combine each pair of sentences using a relative clause.
questions.reponse: 1. The woman who lives next door is a doctor. 2. The book which/that I bought yesterday is very interesting. 3. The man whose car was stolen called the police. 4. The hotel where we stayed last summer was very comfortable. 5. The teacher who teaches English is very kind.

enonce.texte:
Find and correct the errors in the following sentences.

1. The man which is speaking is my boss.

2. She is the woman who car was stolen.

3. This is the book who I wanted to read.

4. The hotel that we stayed was very nice.

5. The teacher which teaches math is very strict.

questions.texte: Correct the errors in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. The man who is speaking is my boss. 2. She is the woman whose car was stolen. 3. This is the book which/that I wanted to read. 4. The hotel where we stayed was very nice. (or The hotel that we stayed in was very nice.) 5. The teacher who teaches math is very strict.

enonce.texte:
Rewrite the sentences using inversion for emphasis.

1. I had never seen such a beautiful sunset before.

2. She has never been so happy.

3. He didn't realize the danger until it was too late.

4. They had just arrived when the storm started.

5. I have never felt so proud.

questions.reponse: 1. Never had I seen such a beautiful sunset before. 2. Never has she been so happy. 3. Not until it was too late did he realize the danger. 4. Hardly had they arrived when the storm started. 5. Never have I felt so proud.

enonce.texte:
Rewrite the sentences as cleft sentences using It is/was... that...

1. I need a new computer.

2. She met him in Paris.

3. We finished the project on time.

4. He wants a new car.

5. They bought the house last year.

questions.texte: Rewrite each sentence as a cleft sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. It is a new computer that I need. 2. It was in Paris that she met him. 3. It was on time that we finished the project. 4. It is a new car that he wants. 5. It was last year that they bought the house.

enonce.texte: Write sentences about your family, friends, or hometown using the following relative pronouns: who, which, that, whose, where.

questions.texte: Write 5 sentences using each relative pronoun.
questions.reponse:
Example answers: 
1. My mother, who is a teacher, works hard. (who)
2. This is the book which I love most. (which)
3. The man that I met yesterday is from Cameroon. (that)
4. My friend, whose brother is a pilot, travels a lot. (whose)
5. This is the school where I studied. (where)

enonce.texte:
Combine the following information into one complex sentence using relative clauses and/or inversion.

1. The professor is very famous. He wrote many books. He won a Nobel Prize.

2. The city is beautiful. It has many historical monuments. I visited it.

3. The woman is a famous artist. Her paintings are exhibited worldwide. She lives in Paris.

questions.texte: Combine each set of sentences into one complex sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. The professor, who wrote many books and won a Nobel Prize, is very famous. 2. The city, which has many historical monuments and which I visited, is beautiful. 3. The woman, whose paintings are exhibited worldwide and who lives in Paris, is a famous artist.

enonce.texte:
Identify and correct the errors in the following complex sentences.

1. The man who he is standing there is my uncle.

2. This is the house which I was born.

3. She is the person whom I told you about her.

4. The book which I read it was very interesting.

5. The students which passed the exam will receive a certificate.

questions.texte: Correct the errors in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. The man who is standing there is my uncle. 2. This is the house where I was born. 3. She is the person whom I told you about. 4. The book which I read was very interesting. 5. The students who passed the exam will receive a certificate.

enonce.texte: Write a short story (100-150 words) about a memorable travel experience. Use at least five different relative clauses and at least one cleft sentence or inversion for emphasis.

questions.texte: Write a short story using relative clauses and advanced structures.
questions.reponse:
Example answer: 
It was in 2018 that I travelled to Yaoundé for the first time. The city, which is the capital of Cameroon, was more vibrant than I had expected. My cousin, who lives there, showed me around the city. The markets, which are full of colorful fabrics and fresh food, were my favorite places to visit. The people, whose hospitality is well-known, made me feel welcome. It was at the Mvog-Mbi Zoo that I saw the most beautiful animals. Never had I felt so connected to nature. The trip, which lasted two weeks, was truly unforgettable. I will always remember the friend who guided me through this adventure.
